description: Synthetic denial-chart pairs for DenialDefender pipeline development and testing
payers: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois

cases.appeal_strategy_notes: Strong case — patient has documented foot drop (motor deficit = red flag), failed conservative treatment, and X-ray already obtained. Denial cites insufficient PT duration but overlooks neurological emergency. Appeal should emphasize motor deficit, cite AAN/NASS/ACR guidelines, and argue red-flag exception to the 6-week PT requirement.

Administrative denial — medical necessity not disputed. Provider office admits PA was an administrative oversight. Patient was not notified PA was missing. Appeal should request retroactive authorization, cite CA balance billing protections (H&S Code §1371.8), and argue patient hold-harmless since provider failed to notify.

cases.procedure: Continuous Glucose Monitor — Dexcom G7 (HCPCS A9278, S1037)
cases.appeal_strategy_notes: Plan exclusion based on insulin regimen complexity, but patient has hypoglycemia unawareness with 2 severe nocturnal episodes — a safety-critical indication. Appeal should cite ADA Standards of Care 2026 (CGM for all insulin users at hypoglycemia risk), Endocrine Society guidelines, and argue medical exception for patient safety. Alternatively, physician may transition to basal-bolus to independently satisfy plan criteria.

Straightforward coding fix. Provider submitted I25.10 (CAD) instead of R06.00 (dyspnea), R01.1 (murmur), and I35.0 (aortic stenosis). Corrected claim resubmission with proper dx codes should resolve. No appeal needed — just corrected claim with frequency code 7.

cases.payer: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois
cases.appeal_strategy_notes: Most complex case. Patient has significant pre-existing cardiac disease (myocarditis hx, AFib, moderate MR, borderline EF). Dosimetric comparison is dramatic (16x MHD reduction). Appeal should cite Darby et al. cardiac risk data, patient-specific cardiac comorbidities, cardiology letter supporting PBRT, PTCOG consensus, and argue that denying PBRT exposes patient to unacceptable cardiac risk. External IRO review recommended.
